titre: Disabled child education allowance (AEEH) and the MDPH
resume: Putting together a complete file at the MDPH de La Réunion for the AEEH: form, medical certificate less than a year old, exact documents, response time and appeals.
aQuoiCaSert: The AEEH (allocation d'éducation de l'enfant handicapé, disabled child education allowance) helps parents cover the education and care costs of a child with a disability. It consists of a basic amount to which a supplement may be added, depending on the child's needs and the impact on the parents' work. You apply to the MDPH (maison départementale des personnes handicapées, the local disability services center). The CDAPH (commission des droits et de l'autonomie, the rights and autonomy committee) decides, then the Caf de La Réunion (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office) pays the allowance.
quiEstConcerne: Parents of a child under 20 with a disability rate of at least 80%.
Parents of a child with a rate from 50% to under 80%, if the child is followed by a medical and social service, receives adapted schooling or care.
Separated parents, whatever the child's residence arrangement.
aSavoir: Basic amount: €153.01 per month. Supplements are added depending on the category of disability and the impact on the parent's work (service-public.gouv.fr).
The medical certificate (cerfa n° 15695) must be no more than one year old when you submit the file.
The CDAPH has 4 months to decide. With no reply after 4 months, the application is considered rejected.

If refused: mandatory prior administrative appeal (recours administratif préalable obligatoire) to the MDPH within 2 months, then, with no reply or if rejected, an appeal to the tribunal judiciaire (judicial court) where you live within 2 months.
Duration: 3 to 5 years if the rate is at least 80%, 2 to 5 years between 50 and 80%, or with no limit until age 20 if the child's condition cannot improve.
Under shared residence, the AEEH is not shared: it is paid in full to the parent designated as the beneficiary (rule for family benefits other than family allowances).
A law of June 12, 2026 provides for a trial to shorten processing times, with an automatic advance when the CDAPH has not replied. It only applies once the decrees are published.

documents.detail: Original, dated and signed by the legal representative. Available on service-public.gouv.fr or from the MDPH.

documents.libelle: Medical certificate (cerfa n° 15695) less than a year old
documents.detail: Original completed by the doctor who follows the child. Attach any useful reports (assessments, tests).

documents.libelle: ID document (front and back) or residence permit
documents.detail: Valid photocopy, for the child and for the legal representative.
Photocopy. If you are housed by someone, add a sworn statement (attestation sur l'honneur) from the person housing you.

documents.libelle: Protection judgment or decision on parental authority, if applicable
documents.detail: Copy, if a decision sets who exercises parental authority or if a protection measure exists.
Copies. The form includes optional sections for hearing and eye assessments.

documents.libelle: MDPH acknowledgment of receipt of the file
documents.detail: Keep it: it starts the 4-month period.

etapes.titre: Make an appointment with the doctor for the medical certificate
etapes.detail: It must be less than a year old when you submit. Ask the doctor to detail the child's everyday needs.
Describe the child's life, needs, schooling and your expenses. The life plan (projet de vie) helps the committee understand the situation.
Signed form, original medical certificate less than a year old, IDs, proof of address, any judgment, assessments. An incomplete file delays the review.

etapes.titre: Send the file to the MDPH de La Réunion
etapes.detail: Preferably by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt, or online if the MDPH offers it. Keep a full copy.
Note the submission date: with no reply after 4 months, follow up; if refused, appeal within 2 months.

ou.detail: Contact details to check in the official Mon Parcours Handicap directory.
Pays the AEEH after the CDAPH decision.
